analysis: Uniform unique-item history weighting achieved host validation macro HR@10 of 0.5363, improving over the prior recency-weighted result of 0.5212 by 0.0151. Per-category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.575, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.535, Electronics 0.355, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.680. Electronics improved from 0.325 but remained below the historical SASRec result of 0.420. The outcome supports retaining uniform weighting for this configuration; it does not establish that recency weighting is generally harmful. The result is slightly above the historical uniform-history MultVAE score of 0.535, without evidence of statistical significance. No test metrics were available.
code_summary: Per-category MultVAE with sorted, deduplicated history IDs weighted equally by 1/sqrt(K). A weighted EmbeddingBag produces a 256-dimensional encoder representation after input dropout of 0.5 and tanh; the posterior has 64-dimensional Gaussian latent variables. A tanh decoder hidden layer feeds item logits. Training uses binary multinomial reconstruction plus annealed KL, Adam, gradient clipping, and validation-selected checkpoints. Inference uses the deterministic posterior mean. The generated predictor shares history transformation and architecture loading with training, preserving all four dataset routes and trial-local artifacts.
